title: Evelyn & Danny

questions.text:
Danny's been my whole life since he was twelve. I just want to understand him again.
Every night, past eleven, his phone lights up and he takes it out on the porch.
I can hear him through the screen door, keeping his voice low. 😔
Who keeps calling Danny that late at night?

That boy's practically my second grandson.
They've been thick as thieves since third grade. He still calls me Mamaw Ev.
Danny tells me he's out on sales calls all day, every day.
Where does Danny actually go when he says he's on sales calls?

Lord. Ten minutes over the bridge, and I never knew. 😳
His granddaddy lost a whole paycheck at the track once, and I never let him forget it.
At supper Danny's thumb never stops, and he groans at ballgames he isn't even watching.
Which betting app has Danny been using?

So it's in his pocket too. Day and night.
I balance my checkbook to the penny every week. He knows that, and he hid this from me anyway.
How many times has Danny put money into BetHarbor over the past 7 days?

That's not a slip-up. That's a habit. 💔
If he's at that casino every day, he can't be at Sunvale.
And his work polo shirts haven't come through my laundry in weeks.
What reason did Sunvale give for letting Danny go?
questions.hint: Check his Mail, beyond the Inbox.

questions.text:
He let me pack him lunches for a job he didn't have.
I never even cashed that check he gave me. It's tucked in my sewing box.
Where did Danny get the $3,000 he gave me?

That's the name on that letter in my drawer. 😳
A lending company means a loan, and a loan has to be paid back.
I've never borrowed a dime in my life, not even for this house.
What kind of loan did Hollis Lending give out?

onboarding.text: A letter came last week from some lending company I've never heard of. Fine print, legal words, and my address at the top. I put it in the kitchen drawer. I haven't slept right since.

onboarding.text: I've raised Danny since he was twelve, right here in our house on Larkspur Lane. He used to sit under my sewing table handing me pins. He still kisses my cheek every morning.
onboarding.label: Evelyn & Danny

onboarding.text: He's twenty-six now. Says he sells solar panels, says business is good. Not long ago he handed me three thousand dollars. But he's thin, jumpy, and on that phone till all hours.
onboarding.label: Danny

onboarding.text: This morning he left for a sales call and forgot his phone on the kitchen counter. I can't make heads or tails of these things. You can. Please, find out what my boy has gotten into.
